items.stem: As data passes down the TCP/IP stack from application to network layer, what happens at each layer?

options.text: Each layer adds its own header, encapsulating the data from the layer above
options.rationale: Correct: encapsulation adds headers as the PDU descends the stack.

options.text: Each layer removes a header added by the layer above
options.rationale: Headers are added going down and removed going up.

options.text: The data is encrypted once at the physical layer
options.rationale: Encapsulation is not encryption and is not limited to one layer.

options.text: Only the application layer touches the data
options.rationale: Every layer adds its header during encapsulation.

items.explanation: Correct: encapsulation adds headers as the PDU descends the stack.

items.stem: Which TWO characteristics describe UDP compared with TCP? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is connectionless, sending datagrams without a handshake
options.rationale: Correct: UDP does not establish a connection before sending.

options.text: It does not guarantee ordered, reliable delivery
options.rationale: Correct: UDP provides no retransmission or ordering guarantees.

options.text: It uses a three-way handshake to open a connection
options.rationale: The handshake is a TCP feature, not UDP.
Congestion control is a TCP mechanism, not UDP.

items.explanation: Correct: UDP does not establish a connection before sending.

items.stem: A host has IP 192.168.1.10 with mask 255.255.255.0. How many usable host addresses exist on its subnet?

options.text: 254, because 8 host bits give 256 addresses minus network and broadcast
256, counting every address in the range
options.rationale: The network and broadcast addresses are not usable hosts.
Both the network and broadcast addresses are excluded.
